lung.label: Lung cancer
lung.question: Do you often experience a persistent cough, coughing up blood, chest pain, and shortness of breath?

breast.label: Breast cancer
breast.question: Do you often experience symptoms of hard lumps, skin dimpling, swelling, and nipple discharge?
breast.specialist: a primary care doctor, who can order a mammogram or ultrasound

colorectal.label: Colorectal cancer
colorectal.question: Do you often experience changes in bowel habits, blood in the stool, and ongoing abdominal discomfort?

urinary.label: Prostate, bladder or kidney cancer
urinary.question: Do you often experience trouble urinating, weak urine flow, or blood in the urine?

skin.label: Skin cancer (melanoma)
skin.question: Do you often experience asymmetrical moles, irregular borders, changing colors, or sores that do not heal?

blood.label: Blood cancer (leukemia or lymphoma)
blood.question: Do you often experience easy bruising or bleeding, swollen lymph nodes, and frequent infections?
blood.specialist: a blood doctor (hematologist), after a blood test from your primary care doctor

liver_pancreas.label: Pancreatic or liver cancer
liver_pancreas.question: Do you often experience yellowing of the skin and eyes (jaundice), upper abdominal pain, and pale stools?
liver_pancreas.specialist: a primary care doctor today (yellow skin or eyes needs a check soon), then a liver or digestive specialist

screenings.name: Colorectal cancer screening
screenings.how: A stool test (FIT) every year, or a colonoscopy every 10 years
screenings.status: verified final recommendation; individual exceptions apply

screenings.name: Mammogram
screenings.status: verified final recommendation; individual exceptions apply

screenings.name: Cervical cancer screening
screenings.how: Pap every 3 years at ages 21–29; ages 30–65: Pap every 3 years, HPV every 5 years, or co-testing every 5 years (USPSTF 2018)
screenings.status: verified final recommendation; individual exceptions apply

screenings.name: Prostate (PSA) test
screenings.how: Talk with a doctor and decide together
screenings.status: verified final recommendation; individual exceptions apply

screenings.name: Low-dose CT lung scan
screenings.who: Adults with at least 20 pack-years who currently smoke or quit within 15 years
screenings.how: Annual low-dose CT for eligible people without symptoms; confirm benefits, harms and suitability with a clinician
screenings.status: verified final recommendation; individual exceptions apply

free_screening.name: Washington Breast, Cervical, and Colon Health Program
free_screening.who: Eligibility depends on insurance, income, age and service. Contact the state program to confirm
free_screening.contact: Use the Washington Department of Health program contact directory
free_screening.status: program existence verified; numerical eligibility limits removed

screening_context.status: verified report figures; not individual risk
